summary: For ages 5–7, build awareness and wonder that the ocean is a huge body of salty water covering most of Earth's surface and home to an enormous variety of living things. Core moves: let children SEE on a globe/world map that there is more blue (ocean) than green (land); anchor 'salty' to sensory memory and contrast with the fresh water of taps, rivers and lakes; and reveal the teeming life beneath the surface. Keep quantities qualitative ('most', 'huge') at this age.
misconceptions: 'There's more land than sea' — the ocean covers most of Earth (about 71%).
'Ocean water is like the water we drink' — it is salty and unsafe to drink, unlike fresh river/lake/tap water.
'The sea is just a big puddle / empty water' — it is vast, deep, and full of more life than land.
'Seas and oceans are totally separate pools' — the ocean is really one connected body of water around the world.
'Only fish live in the ocean' — mammals, invertebrates, plants/algae and countless others live there too.

activities.title: Meet the ocean: globe reveal, salt flap, and dive-in
steps: Look at a globe or world map and point to the blue parts (water) and the land parts (often green or brown — check the map's colours); say out loud which there is more of.
Lift a flap or reveal panel on the water to meet the question 'Why can't you drink it?' and hear the salt fact, with a river or tap pictured alongside for contrast.

'Dive in' beneath the waves (turn a page, open an underwater scene, or tap a drill-down panel) to discover a world packed with creatures of many shapes and sizes — whales, fish, crabs, jellyfish, seahorses.
activities.insight: Our planet's surface is mostly ocean; ocean water is salty (unlike the fresh water we drink); and the ocean is home to a huge variety of living things.

activities.title: Paint the globe / sort the water (hands-on scaffold)
steps: Paint or place blue tiles over the water parts of a world outline and green over the land, then look at how much more blue there is.
Sort pictures or labels of water sources into two groups: salty (the sea/ocean) and fresh (river, lake, tap).
activities.insight: 'Most of Earth is ocean' and 'salty vs fresh' become felt through doing, not just seen.

activities.title: Talk it through: how is the ocean different from a lake?
steps: Respond to: 'A lake is big too. Name one thing that makes the OCEAN different from a big lake.' (Looking for salt and/or vast scale.)
Decide and explain: 'Is there just one ocean or lots of separate ones — what do you think?' then look at a globe to see the water is really one connected body wrapping the planet.

Answer the challenge: 'Someone says the ocean is just a really big lake, the water is the same as a river, and there's more land than ocean. Are they right? Tell me one way ocean water is different, and whether land or ocean covers more of Earth.'
activities.insight: The ocean is distinguished from familiar water (puddles, pools, ponds, rivers, lakes) by its saltiness and its vast, connected scale — and both facts can be held at once.

checkQuestion: Someone says: 'The ocean is just a really big lake — the water is the same as the water in a river, and there's more land on Earth than ocean anyway.' Are they right? Tell me one way ocean water is different from river water, and whether land or ocean covers more of the Earth.
checkAnswer: They're not right on either count. Ocean water is SALTY, while river and lake water is fresh (not salty) — that's why you can't drink sea water. And the ocean covers MORE of the Earth than land does (about two-thirds / most of the planet's surface is ocean).
